GENERAL PROVISIONS
§ 30.01 SHORT TITLE.
   This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the “Administrative Code of
the City of Bowling Green, Ohio,” or the “administrative code.”
(1980 Code, § 30.01) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.02 DEFINITIONS.
   For the purposes of this chapter, the following definitions shall apply
unless the context clearly indicates or requires a different meaning.
   CITY. The City of Bowling Green, Ohio.
   CITY COUNCIL or COUNCIL. The Council of the City of Bowling Green, Ohio.
   HEAD OF DEPARTMENT or DEPARTMENT HEAD. The director of a department and, in
the case of the Department of Public Utilities, the Board of Public Utilities.
(1980 Code, § 30.02) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.03 INDEMNIFICATION OF CITY PERSONNEL.
   (A)   On and after November 1, 1985, all city personnel, including but not
limited to all elected officials, all appointed officials, all members of
boards and commissions, all members of ad-hoc committees appointed by the Mayor
or City Council, all classified and unclassified employees of the city
including police, fire, paramedics, and advanced emergency medical technicians,
shall be indemnified by the city for individual liability for work performed in
the scope of their employment for the city to the extent that such personnel
are presently covered under the existing Public Officials and Employees
Liability Policy, being policy number 524-014431-3, issued by International
Surplus Lines Insurance Company, which policy covers only monetary damages and
does not cover bodily injury or property damage. The indemnification shall be
100% of the policy limits and no deductible shall apply.
   (B)   This indemnification shall be enlarged to a $1,000,000 limit
regardless of coverage put forth in the policy described in division (A) above.
   (C)   The indemnification as set forth above shall continue to be provided
even though the city obtains additional coverage under a Public Officials and
Employees Liability Policy.
(1980 Code, § 30.03) (Ord. 4610, passed 10-28-1985)
Cross-reference:
   Defending and indemnifying employees, see §
37.06
MAYOR
§ 30.05 ELECTION AND TERM.
   (A)   The Mayor shall be elected at the regular municipal election held in
the year 1975 and every fourth year thereafter, for a term of four years.
   (B)   His or her term shall commence and he or she shall assume office on
January 1 next following the election. He or she shall serve until his or her
successor is elected and qualified.
(1980 Code, § 30.05) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
Charter reference:
   Election and term, see Charter, §
3.01
§ 30.06 SEAL OF THE CITY.
   The seal of the Mayor shall be the official seal of the city.
(1980 Code, § 30.06) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.07 CHIEF EXECUTIVE.
   The Mayor shall be the chief executive and administrator of the city
government. He or she shall enforce the laws of the city and require the
faithful performance of all administrative duties, and shall perform the duties
and exercise the powers provided hereinafter.
(1980 Code, § 30.07) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
Charter reference:
   Executive powers, see Charter, §
3.05
§ 30.08 DUTIES.
   The Mayor shall have the duties as set forth in the charter of the city and
as provided by the Ohio Revised Code. In addition, it shall be the duty of the
Mayor to perform the following.
   (A)   Appoint, dismiss, suspend, discipline.
      (1)   Appoint competent, qualified persons to the administrative service,
and, except as otherwise provided, shall have the power to dismiss, suspend,
and discipline all persons in the administrative service under his or her
control. The City Council shall have the authority to determine which of such
appointees shall be residents of the city and such appointees shall be
residents of the city on assuming their duties and during the period of their
service to the city, but need not be residents at the time of their
appointment. Nonresident persons in the administrative service at the date of
the adoption of this administrative code shall not be required to become
residents.
      (2)   All appointments of the Mayor to the offices of Municipal
Administrator, Finance Director, city attorney, and to any board or commission
of the city shall require the confirmation of Council.
   (B)   Appoint to acting capacity. Designate any person to perform the duties
of any position in the administrative service under his or her control which is
vacant or which lacks administration due to the absence or disability of the
incumbent until the absence or disability ceases.
   (C)   Budget report. Prepare and submit the annual estimate of receipts and
expenditures and of appropriation measures and furnish to the Council full
information on the financial condition and needs of the municipality.
   (D)   Meetings. Attend all meetings of Council unless excused by Council.
   (E)   Contracts. Execute personally or through a designee all contracts on
behalf of the city except those pertaining to the Department of Public
Utilities.
   (F)   Investment. Participate together with the Finance Director and the
city attorney in the decisions regarding the investment of the city funds as
authorized by ordinance and R.C. §§ 731.56 through 731.58.
(1980 Code, § 30.08) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 3815, passed 1-15-
1979)
Cross-reference:
   Executive powers, see Charter, §
3.05
§ 30.09 POWERS.
   The Mayor shall exercise all powers granted by ordinance or state law which
are not inconsistent with the charter, and shall have the power to:
   (A)   Classify and assign according to classification. Classify and place on
the salary schedule any new employee of the city, approve advancements to
higher steps on the schedule and assign any employee of the city to any
department or branch thereof requiring services appropriate to the
classification of the employee so assigned.
   (B)   Prescribe rules. Prescribe those rules and regulations not
inconsistent with the charter or this administrative code which he or she shall
deem necessary or expedient for the conduct of administrative agencies subject
to his or her authority, and he or she shall have the power to revoke, suspend,
or amend any rule or regulation of the administrative agencies subject to his
or her authority.
   (C)   Investigate. Investigate and examine or inquire into the affairs or
operation of any department, division, board, or commission either by himself,
herself or by any person designated for the purpose by him or her; and when so
authorized by the Council, he or she shall have the power to employ consultants
and professional counsel to aid in the investigations, examinations, or
inquiries.
   (D)   Overrule officials. Set aside any action by a department head subject
to removal by the Mayor alone.
   (E)   Delegate duties. Direct any department or division under his or her
control to perform the work for any other department or division.
   (F)   Appoint administrative committees. Designate from the administrative
service those committees and the officers thereof which he or she shall find
necessary for the proper consideration of administrative problems. The
committees shall meet at the request of the Mayor and shall make those
recommendations on matters referred to them which they shall find necessary for
the best interests of the city.
   (G)   Participation in Council. Take part in the discussion upon all matters
under consideration by Council but have no vote therein. Introduce and propose
ordinances and resolutions and, if the adoption of the same shall be moved by a
member of Council, they shall be considered and acted upon as if introduced and
proposed by a member of Council.
   (H)   Approval or veto. Approve or veto every ordinance and resolution of
Council. The Mayor may approve or disapprove in the manner provided below the
whole or any item appropriating money, and the item so disapproved shall be
void unless repassed by Council in the manner herein prescribed. On all non-
appropriation legislation, his or her approval or disapproval shall cover the
entire ordinance or resolution.
      (1)   Approval. If the Mayor approves an ordinance or resolution, he or
she shall sign and return it within ten days after its passage or adoption by
Council.
      (2)   Disapproval. If the Mayor does not approve an ordinance or
resolution, he or she shall return it to the Council within ten days after its
passage or adoption together with a written statement of his or her objections,
which statement shall be entered in its entirety on the journal of Council. Not
later than 30 days after the date upon which the Mayor returned the same to
Council with his or her objections, the Council may reconsider the legislation.
Upon reconsideration, if the legislation is approved by at least two-thirds of
the members of Council, it shall take effect at the time of the vote of the
approval or at a later date specified in the ordinance or resolution.
      (3)   Inaction. If any ordinance or resolution shall not be returned by
the Mayor within ten days after its passage or adoption by Council, it shall
become effective in the same manner as if he or she had signed it on the last
day of the ten-day period.
(1980 Code, § 30.09) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)

   There shall be a Municipal Administrator who shall be appointed by the Mayor
with the approval of a majority of the members of Council. The Municipal
Administrator shall serve at the pleasure of the Mayor. He or she shall be the
principal managerial aide to the Mayor and shall perform the duties assigned to
him or her by the Mayor.
(1980 Code, § 30.12) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)

§ 30.13 QUALIFICATIONS.
   The Municipal Administrator shall be chosen solely on the basis of his or
her executive, administrative, and managerial qualifications as judged by the
adequacy of his or her training and his or her successful experience in private
or public administration. At the time of his or her appointment, he or she need
not be a resident of the city or state, but during regular municipal election
held in the year his or her tenure of office he or she shall reside in the
city.
(1980 Code, § 30.13) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)

§ 30.14 RESIGNATION OR REMOVAL OF THE ADMINISTRATOR.
   (A)   The Administrator shall serve for an indefinite term, subject to
removal by the Mayor after he or she has served six months. If removed at any
time after he or she has served six months, he or she may demand the right to
be heard thereon at a public meeting of the Council prior to 30 days before the
removal shall become effective, but pending and during the hearing the Mayor
may suspend him or her from office and designate an acting Administrator in
accordance with the provisions of the original appointment.
   (B)   In the case of the voluntary resignation of the Administrator, the
Mayor and the Administrator shall agree upon the effective date of the
resignation.
   (C)   Upon removal, unless for misconduct involving moral turpitude, he or
she shall be paid his or her salary for the period of the next month following
the removal.
(1980 Code, § 30.14) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)

§ 30.22 ADMINISTRATIVE POLICY AND PROCEDURES.
   (A)   Bureaus and Departments. Each bureau and department shall furnish,
upon the direction of the Mayor, any other department the service, labor, and
material requisitioned by the head of the department, as its own facilities
permit, through the same procedure and subject to the same audit and control as
other expenditures are incurred.
   (B)   Bureau directors. The director of each bureau shall:
      (1)   Be responsible to the Mayor. Be immediately responsible to the
Mayor for the effective administration of their respective bureau and all
activities assigned thereto.
      (2)   Inaugurate sound practices. Keep informed as to the latest
practices in their particular field and inaugurate, with the approval of the
Mayor, those new practices which appear to be of benefit to the service and to
the public.
      (3)   Report to the Mayor. Report to the Mayor as required or found
necessary by the Mayor.
      (4)   Establish rules. Establish rules and regulations for the management
and operation of their bureau.
   (C)   Department heads. The heads of departments shall:
      (1)   Be responsible to the Mayor, under the supervision of the
respective bureau director. Be immediately responsible to the Mayor for the
effective administration of their respective departments and all activities
assigned thereto.
      (2)   Inaugurate sound practices. Keep informed as to the latest
practices in their particular field and inaugurate, with the approval of the
Mayor, those new practices which appear to be of benefit to the service and to
the public.
      (3)   Report to the Mayor. Report to the Mayor as required or found
necessary by the Mayor.
      (4)   Maintain records. Establish and maintain a system of filing and
indexing records and reports in sufficient detail to furnish all information
necessary for the proper control of departmental activities and to form a basis
for the periodic reports to the Mayor.
      (5)   Establish rules. Establish rules and regulations for the management
and operation of their departments.
(1980 Code, § 30.22) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 8920, passed 5-17-
2021)
Charter reference:
   Administrative code, see Charter, §
6.04

§ 30.24 BUREAU DIRECTORS.
   Each bureau shall have assigned to it an executive director who shall be
responsible for the day-to-day management, supervision, and accomplishment of
the departments assigned. Additionally, upon approval of the Mayor and when
applicable, City Council, the bureau directors shall be responsible for setting
the strategic direction and review of the respective departments. Upon approval
of the Mayor, the bureau directors may be assigned contracting authority not to
exceed the established bid limit threshold.
(Ord. 8920, passed 5-17-2021)
DEPARTMENT OF LAW
§ 30.25 CITY ATTORNEY.
   The appointing authority and head of the Department of Law shall be the city
attorney, who shall be appointed by the Mayor for an indefinite term, subject
to confirmation by a majority of the members of Council. The city attorney may
be removed by the Mayor with the approval of a majority of the members of
Council.
(1980 Code, § 30.25) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
Charter reference:
   Department of Law, see Charter, §
6.06
§ 30.26 DUTIES.
   The city attorney shall:
   (A)   Advise Council and others. Advise the Council or its committees, the
Mayor, or department heads when requested, upon all legal questions arising in
the conduct of city business.
   (B)   Prepare ordinances. Prepare or revise ordinances when so requested by
the Mayor or by the Council or any committee thereof.
   (C)   Give opinions; provide representation. Give his or her opinion upon
any legal matter or question submitted to him or her by the Council, any of its
committees, the Mayor, department heads, Planning Commission, or the Board of
Zoning Appeals.
   (D)   Attend Council meetings. Unless unavoidably detained, attend all
Council meetings in their entirety for the purpose of giving the Council any
legal advice requested by its members.
   (E)   Prepare legal instruments. Prepare for execution all contracts and
instruments to which the city is a party and shall approve, as to form, all
bonds required to be submitted to the city.
   (F)   Prosecute offenders and defend the city and its agents. Propose, when
authorized by the Council, all charges and complaints against the city, and
appear in the appropriate court in the prosecution of, every person charged
with the violation of a city ordinance or of any regulations adopted under
authority of the charter.
   (G)   Settlement of claims. Have the power to adjust, settle, compromise, or
submit to arbitration any action, causes of action, accounts, debts, claims,
demands, disputes, and matters of favor of or against the city or in which the
city is concerned as debtor or creditor, now existing or which may hereafter
arise, not involving or requiring payment to exceed $1,500, and with the
permission of the Mayor may do likewise in matters not involving or requiring
payment to exceed $5,000 provided the money to settle claims generally has been
appropriated and is available therefor.
   (H)   Make reports.
      (1)   Immediate report of decision. Immediately report to the Mayor and
Council the outcome of any litigation in which the city has an interest.
      (2)   Annual report of pending litigation. Make an annual report to the
Mayor and Council, as of March 1, of all pending litigation in which the city
has an interest and the condition thereof.
   (I)   Control legal services incidental to Council action. Have charge of
all legal services auxiliary to Council action in connection with the
appropriating of property to public use and the levying of assessments.
   (J)   Keep records.
      (1)   Suits. Keep a complete record of all actions in which the city had
or has an interest, giving the names of the parties, the court where brought,
the nature of the action, the disposition of the case (or its condition if
pending), and the briefs of counsel.
      (2)   Opinions and titles. Keep a complete record of all written opinions
furnished by him or her and of all certificates or abstracts of titles
furnished by him or her to the city or any department thereof.
   (K)   Deliver records to successor. Deliver all records, documents, and
properties of every description in his or her possession, belonging to his or
her office or to the city, to his or her successor in office, who shall give
him or her duplicate receipts therefor, one of which he or she shall file with
the Finance Director.
   (L)   Represent departments. Represent all departments, divisions, and
agencies of the city in any proceedings before courts or administrative
agencies.
   (M)   Appoint assistant city attorney. Appoint the assistant city attorney
and those other employees of the Department of Law authorized by Council.
   (N)   Participate in investment. Participate together with the Mayor and
Finance Director in decisions regarding the investment of city funds as
authorized by ordinance and R.C. §§ 731.56 through 731.58.
(1980 Code, § 30.26) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.27 SPECIAL COMPENSATION.
   The compensation provided for the city attorney in the basic salary
ordinance of the city shall cover all his or her duties except those in
connection with proceedings and appearances before the common pleas courts and
higher courts or before county or state boards, and except those in connection
with the preparation of assessments and the issuance of notes and bonds. The
city attorney’s special compensation shall be at the usual and customary hourly
rate for these services.
(1980 Code, § 30.27) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.28 ASSISTANT CITY ATTORNEY.
   The assistant city attorney shall be the prosecutor of the municipal court,
shall assist the city attorney, and shall perform those duties the city
attorney shall prescribe.
(1980 Code, § 30.28) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.29 SPECIAL COUNSEL.
   The city attorney shall have the authority to designate and contract with
special counsel to render legal services to the city in connection with
litigation, note and bond proceedings, special assessment proceedings, and
other legal matters which in the opinion of the city attorney can be performed
best by special counsel.
(1980 Code, § 30.29) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)

   The appointing authority and head of the Department of Finance shall be the

(1980 Code, § 30.35) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
Charter reference:
   Department of Finance, see Charter, §
6.05
§ 30.351 LIABILITY FOR LOSS OF PUBLIC FUNDS.
   The Finance Director, or other officer of the municipality having the duties
of a treasurer or of a city auditor, shall not be held liable for a loss of
public funds when the officer has performed all official duties required of the
officer with reasonable care, but shall be liable only when a loss of public
funds results from the officer's negligence or other wrongful act.
(R.C. § 733.82)
§ 30.36 DUTIES.
   The Finance Director shall be the fiscal officer of the city, and shall
perform the following duties.
   (A)   Account and collect funds. Be responsible for the accounting,
collection, and custody of funds and control over disbursements.
   (B)   Execute bonds and notes. Execute all bonds and notes issued by the
city in the manner provided by law.
   (C)   Fiscal supervision. Exercise general supervision over all departments
of the city regarding the proper management of their fiscal concerns.
      (1)   Examine books. Examine the books of each department from time to
time, and see that they are kept in proper form.
      (2)   Report delinquent payments and financial reports. See that
personnel receiving money pay the same into the city treasury, when thereto
required, and that all necessary financial reports are made, and report all
delinquents in such payments or reports to the Mayor and Council.
   (D)   Duty upon default. Report the fiscal default of any personnel of the
city to the Mayor who shall direct the city attorney to take immediate legal
measures for the recovery of the amount which may be in default.
   (E)   Responsibility for proceeds of bonds. Deposit the proceeds of all
sales of bonds in those funds as provided by law immediately after he or she
shall have received the same, and, until the deposit, be responsible for the
amount thereof.
   (F)   Payments of money from special trust funds. Pay out to the persons
duly entitled thereto, without appropriation by the Council, any money paid
into the treasury pursuant to condemnation proceedings, or for the redemption
of property sold for taxes, or arising from special assessments for public
improvements, park fund certificates, condemnation fund certificates, and all
special trust funds except revenue sharing.
   (G)   Responsibility for the investment, including responsibility for the
determination and distribution of interest earnings in accordance with city
policy and R.C. § 135.21, and/or its successors. Prepare fiscal statements,
make recommendations, participate in decisions, and maintain records regarding
the investment of city funds as authorized by ordinance and R.C. §§ 731.56
through 731.58, or its successors.
(1980 Code, § 30.36) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 5939, passed 12-18-
1995)
§ 30.37 DIVISIONS OF DEPARTMENT OF FINANCE.
   The Department of Finance shall be divided into a division of accounting and
a division of income tax.
(1980 Code, § 30.37) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.38 DIVISION OF ACCOUNTING.
   The head of the division of accounting shall be the commissioner of
accounting who shall perform the following duties.
   (A)   Accounts of receipts and expenditures. Keep in proper books a full and
accurate account of all the monies received and disbursed by him or her in
behalf of the city, specifying the time of receipt and disbursement, from whom
received and to whom disbursed and on what account received and disbursed, and
how paid.
   (B)   Receive and disburse monies. Receive and have custody of all monies
paid to the city including income tax payments, and disburse city monies.
   (C)   Pay city employees. Pay city employees upon presentation of the
properly certified payroll.
   (D)   Collect monies and fees due city. Demand and receive all monies and
fees owing to the city whenever any person is indebted to the city in any
manner, and the means of collection of the debt is not otherwise provided for
by law. When any claim shall not be collectible by other methods, report the
same to the city attorney for prosecution.
   (E)   Permits and licenses. Issue all permits and licenses except those
which are required by ordinance to be issued by a particular department.
   (F)   Monthly report to Finance Director. Make a detailed report to the
Finance Director, on the first day of each month, as to the business of his or
her office during the month preceding, showing the balance on hand to the
credit of the different funds at the time of his or her last report, the
amounts received during the month, and on what account, together with such
other items and facts as the Finance Director may require.
   (G)   Audit accounts. Examine and audit the accounts of all personnel and
departments.
   (H)   Prescribe form. Prescribe the form of financial accounts and reports
to be rendered to him or her.
   (I)   Certify contracts. Certify according to law the availability of funds
to meet all contracts, agreements, or other obligations for the expenditure of
public funds entered into by the city; and no such contract, agreement, or
other obligation shall be valid until so certified by him or her.
   (J)   Budget duties. Prepare estimates of revenue, and give other assistance
in the preparation of the budget as required of him or her by the Mayor.
   (K)   Financial statements. Transmit to the Mayor, at least monthly, audited
statements of cash on hand and of classified unencumbered appropriation
balances for the city as a whole, and those other financial statements the
Mayor may from time to time require. Keep all departments, boards, commissions,
or institutions currently informed of its classified unencumbered appropriation
balances.
   (L)   Keep accounts. Keep all general accounts of the city government and of
the respective departments, divisions, boards, commissions, and institutions
thereof.
   (M)   Custodian of bonds, contracts. Be charged with the custody of the
official bonds of city employees, except his or her own, which shall be in the
custody of the Mayor, and with the custody of all deeds, mortgages, contracts,
judgments, notes, debts, and choses in action. Keep and administer all
securities, bonds, or other forms of negotiable instruments owned by or
belonging to the city.
   (N)   Prepare assessment rolls. Prepare assessment lists and other work in
connection with the assessment of property for public improvements and
services, and the preparation of all assessment and tax rolls and tax notices.

§ 30.50 ORGANIZATION; MEETINGS.
   At the annual meeting of the Board of Public Utilities, it shall organize by
the designation of one of the Board members to act as chairperson and another
to act as secretary. The chairperson shall preside at all meetings when
present, and shall call special meetings on his or her own motion or when
requested to do so by two other Board members. The secretary shall keep a
record of the proceedings which shall be available for inspection as other
municipal records.
(1980 Code, § 30.50) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.51 QUORUM; ATTENDANCE.
   (A)   A majority of the Board of Public Utilities shall constitute a quorum.
   (B)   Any Board member failing to attend four successive meetings without
excuse acceptable to and approved by the Board of Public Utilities shall be
removed from office automatically thereby, and the vacancy shall be filled as
hereinbefore provided.
(1980 Code, § 30.51) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.52 DUTIES.
   It shall be the duty of the Board of Public Utilities to perform the
following.
   (A)   Manage and control. Manage and control the operation of the municipal
electric, waterworks, and sewerage systems.
   (B)   Administer contracts. Administer and carry out the provisions of all
agreements, contracts, trust indentures, and other legal obligations pertaining
to the municipal utility systems.
   (C)   Maintain equipment. Control and maintain all property and equipment of
the several systems.
   (D)   Fix rates. Fix all rates and charges to be made to the consumers of
the waterworks, electric, and sewerage systems.
   (E)   Carry out Council directives. Carry out directives of Council
regarding specific improvements to be made to the municipal utilities systems,
including installation of additional street lights and fire hydrants.
   (F)   Bill customers, account for monies. Bill customers of the public
utility systems, receive, account for, and pay over to the Department of
Finance all monies derived from the operation of the municipal electric,
waterworks, and sewerage systems.
   (G)   Approve payments. Approve for payment all expenses and wages incurred
in the usual operation, maintenance, and improvement of the several systems.
   (H)   Keep records. Keep adequate records and accounts of all transactions
of each system.
   (I)   Advertise for bids. Advertise for bids on all contracts involving more
than $50,000.
   (J)   Obtain authorization. Obtain authorization from Council for any
improvement, extension, or addition to municipal utility systems estimated to
cost more than $50,000.
(1980 Code, § 30.52) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 3365, passed 10-20-
1975; Am. Ord. 3948, passed 2-19-1980; Am. Ord. 5029, passed 5-1-1989; Am. Ord.
6456, passed 3-15-1999; Am. Ord. 7167, passed 9-15-2003; Am. Ord. 8289, passed
11-18-13)
§ 30.53 POWERS.
   The Board of Public Utilities shall have the power to:
   (A)   Supervise personnel. With approval of the Mayor and in keeping with
the rules and regulations of the Department of Human Resources, employ,
promote, transfer, suspend, reduce, or discharge all employees within the
Department of Public Utilities necessary to operate and maintain each of the
municipal utilities systems in good order and condition.
   (B)   Purchase equipment; limitation. Purchase all materials, supplies, and
equipment necessary to ensure continuity of service in the several systems.
   (C)   Recommend compensation. Recommend the rates of pay and compensation
for each class of employee of each municipal utility system, and recommend the
placement on the salary schedule of new employees of each system.
   (D)   Enter into contracts. Enter into any lease or contract necessary and
desirable for the proper operation of any of the systems subject to bidding
requirements.
   (E)   Sign contracts. Sign all contracts by its chairperson or executive
director.
   (F)   Make improvements. Make improvements and extensions, costing in each
instance not more than $50,000, to the municipal electric, waterworks, and
sewerage systems.
   (G)   Do all usual and proper things. Do any and all things that are usual
and proper under prudent management to operate, maintain, and improve each of
the systems.
(1980 Code, § 30.53) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 3365, passed 10-20-

DEPARTMENT OF SAFETY
§ 30.60 SAFETY DIRECTOR.
   The head of the Department of Safety shall be the Safety Director, who shall
be the executive head of the Divisions of Police and Fire. He or she shall
establish and designate crosswalks, safety zones, traffic lanes, and “no U-
turn” areas; issue licenses as provided by law; regulate parking within the
city; and make and enforce temporary traffic regulations to cover emergencies
or special conditions. The Director shall send a copy of his or her journal
entries concerning traffic matters, within five days of his or her action, to
each member of the Traffic Commission.
(1980 Code, § 30.60) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.61 DIVISIONS OF DEPARTMENT OF SAFETY.

the Division of Fire.

   (B)   Establish rules. Establish rules and regulations for the working

   (C)   Issue licenses. Issue licenses and permits as are required by law.

§ 30.64 ADULT SCHOOL POLICE.

§ 30.65 (RESERVED).
§ 30.66 (RESERVED).
§ 30.67 SPECIAL DUTY FOR POLICE.
   The Safety Director is authorized and directed to enter into written
agreements with public or private organizations for the assignment of police
officers to special police duty with those organizations where, in the opinion
of the Safety Director and the Chief of Police, this duty serves the purpose of
public safety, traffic control, and public welfare. The written agreements
shall be approved by the Safety Director and city attorney, and shall contain,
among others, the following provisions.
   (A)   The police officer shall be specifically assigned to duty by and under
the control of the Chief of Police, and shall at all times be considered as
being on official police duty.
   (B)   The police officer may or may not be in full uniform depending upon
the nature of the assignment.
   (C)   The city will be reimbursed by the public or private organization
requesting the services at a rate determined by the Safety Director.
   (D)   The duties shall be restricted to the limits of the city.
   (E)   The city will agree to furnish manpower only to the extent of its
availability.
   (F)   The agreement shall be subject to cancellation by either party within
30 days.
(1980 Code, § 30.67) (Ord. 3068, passed 12-17-1973; Am. Ord. 3652, passed 11-7-
1977; Am. Ord. 5253, passed 2-19-1991; Am. Ord. 6323, passed 6-15-1998; Am.
Ord. 6904, passed 1-22-2002; Am. Ord. 8121, passed 9-6-2011; Am. Ord. 8390,
passed 12-15-2014)
§ 30.68 DIVISION OF FIRE; STANDARDS OF COVER; STRATEGIC PLAN.
   (A)   The Division of Fire shall be responsible for the prevention of fires,
the protection of life and property against fire, and the provision of
ambulance service for the city.
   (B)   The city formally adopts the Bowling Green Fire Division Standards of
Cover 2017.
   (C)   The city formally adopts the Bowling Green Fire Division 5-Year
Strategic Plan for 2018.
(1980 Code, § 30.68) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Res. 3236, passed 4-15-

§ 30.69 COMMISSIONER OF FIRE.
   The head of the Division of Fire shall be the Commissioner of Fire, who
shall be the Fire Chief and shall perform the following duties.
   (A)   Direct, assign. Direct and control the assigning, stationing,
transferring, and training of all division personnel subject to the approval of
the Safety Director.
   (B)   Establish rules. Establish rules and regulations for the working
conditions, training courses, organization, and operation of the Division of
Fire subject to the approval of the Safety Director.
   (C)   Issue licenses. Issue licenses and permits as are required by law.
   (D)   Investigate fires. The Commissioner of Fire or his or her authorized
representative shall have full power and authority, under the provisions of
R.C. § 737.27, to investigate the cause of fires, examine witnesses, compel the
attendance of witnesses and the production of books and papers, and to do and
perform all other acts necessary for the effective discharge of these duties.
Such officer may administer oaths, make arrests, and enter, for the purpose of
examination, any building which in his or her opinion is in danger from fire.
The officer shall report his or her proceedings to the Council at such times as
are required by law.
(1980 Code, § 30.69) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 4005, passed 7-7-
1980)
§ 30.70 SPECIAL FIRE FIGHTERS.
   Special fire fighters shall be a unit within the Division of Fire appointed
and removed by the Mayor upon recommendation of the Fire Chief, and shall
respond and serve on call when the need arises. Special fire fighters shall
receive the same training as, and serve under the supervision of, the regular
fire fighters.
(1980 Code, § 30.70) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.71 DIVISION OF TRAFFIC ENGINEERING AND SAFETY.
   (A)   There is established a division of traffic engineering and safety
within the Department of Safety, and the Safety Director shall have full powers
granted under R.C. § 737.022.
   (B)   The Safety Director shall have full power to promulgate all traffic
regulations set forth in R.C. § 737.022, including the power to prohibit
parking on streets, alleys, highways, or public property at designated
locations under times and conditions as promulgated by the Safety Director .
All traffic regulations issued by the Safety Director shall immediately become
part of the traffic control file as official signs.
   (C)   The Safety Director shall consult with the Traffic Commission to
determine standard guidelines for normal traffic control and for emergency
traffic control under extreme snow or other conditions that would impede normal
traffic. Traffic control regulations ordered by the Safety Director shall be
reviewed by the Traffic Commission within 90 days of the Safety Director’s
order. All traffic regulations are subject to the procedures promulgated in §
70.66. In emergency conditions the Safety Director shall have the power to
prohibit parking on streets, alleys, highways, or public property at locations
and times determined by the Safety Director independent of any official action
of the Traffic Commission. No such emergency regulation shall remain in effect
for more than 90 days without the approval of the Traffic Commission.
   (D)   Such rules and regulations shall be issued by posting or publishing
them in the same manner as any ordinance of this city.
   (E)   Violation of any rule and regulation shall be a minor misdemeanor and
shall further enable the impounding, towing, or removal of motor vehicles
parked in prohibited areas as provided in §
76.03. The owner of such vehicle shall pay all towing or storage charges
incurred directly to the person or company towing or storing the vehicle and in
addition pay the charges set forth under §
70.33.
(1980 Code, § 30.71) (Ord. 3779, passed 10-2-1978; Am. Ord. 7460, passed 10-3-
2005)

§ 30.95 CREATION.
   The administrative service of the city shall include the commissions hereby
created: Civil Service, Historic Preservation, Housing, Human Relations,
Planning, Records, Sidewalks, Trees, Traffic, Litter Control, Cable Television;
the boards hereby created: Income Tax Board of Review, Parks and Recreation
Board, Taxicab License Board, and Zoning Board of Appeals; and other
commissions and boards as Council may deem necessary.
(1980 Code, § 30.95) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 4456, passed 7-16-
1984; Am. Ord. 4864, passed 4-4-1988; Am. Ord. 5055, passed 8-7-1989; Am. Ord.
8878, passed 3-15-2021)
Charter reference:

7.03
   Civil Service Commission, See Charter, §
7.01
   Planning Commission, see Charter, §
7.02
§ 30.96 MEMBERS; COMPENSATION; TERMS.
   Except as otherwise provided, all members of city boards and commissions
shall be residents of the city with an appropriate variety of backgrounds and
points of view. They shall be appointed by the Mayor, confirmed by Council, be
removed for cause by the Mayor, and shall serve without compensation. Except
with respect to the Civil Service Commission and Board of Public Utilities and
Records Commission, terms of members of the city’s boards and commissions shall
be limited to two successive terms or ten years of successive service,
whichever is longer. Once a member has served a board or commission for the
maximum successive time permitted herein, a discontinuance of service for at
least one year shall be required before the former member may be appointed to
begin a new term on the same board or commission.
(1980 Code, § 30.96) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 5055, passed 8-7-
1989; Am. Ord. 5210, passed 10-1-1990; Am. Ord. 5305, passed 6-17-1991; Am.
Ord. 9147, passed 12-4-2023)
§ 30.97 ORGANIZATION.
   Every city board and commission, except the Planning Commission, shall
organize annually to elect a chairperson, vice-chairperson, and secretary, and
other officers as convenient. The Planning Commission shall organize annually
to elect a chairperson and vice-chairperson, and other officers as convenient,
except that the secretary to the Planning Commission shall be the Planning
Director. Each city board and commission shall adopt rules for the transaction
of business and keep a journal of its proceedings. Only members who are not
city employees may serve as chair of city boards and commissions.
(1980 Code, § 30.97) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 3602, passed 6-6-
1977; Am. Ord. 6825, passed 7-16-2001)
§ 30.98 MEETINGS, QUORUM; OPEN TO PUBLIC, WHEN.
   (A)   Meetings of all city boards and commissions shall be called as needed
by the chairperson, the Mayor, or three members thereof. A majority of the
members of a city board or commission shall constitute a quorum for the
transaction of business.
   (B)   Meetings of all boards and commissions at which any final action is to
be taken or decision rendered shall be open to the public and any action taken
or decision rendered at a meeting from which members of the public are
excluded, except for misconduct, shall be void.
   (C)   A majority vote of the members present at any duly constituted board
or commission meeting is sufficient for the adoption of a motion. When there is
a tie vote the motion fails. All members present will vote “yea” or “nay” on
all motions unless the member or members disqualify themselves for a conflict
of interest on the business before the board or commission. Voting abstentions
on a motion are not permitted unless a conflict of interest exists.
(1980 Code, § 30.98) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 6851, passed 10-1-
2001)
§ 30.99 DUTIES.
   (A)   All city boards and commissions within their areas of responsibility
shall identify needs and problems, recommend programs, projects, and
legislation; promote public understanding; cooperate with local citizens
groups, and governmental bodies; participate in conferences and workshops; and
perform those specific duties delegated by Council.
   (B)   All city boards and commissions (exceptions: Planning Commission,
Board of Public Utilities, Civil Service Commission and Zoning Board of
Appeals, see division (C) below) will notify the Clerk of Council of meetings
no later than the first scheduled meeting of City Council prior to the board or
commission’s scheduled meeting. This notification will include an agenda for
the next meeting, if possible.
   (C)   The Planning Commission, Board of Public Utilities, Civil Service
Commission and Zoning Board of Appeals will forward to the Mayor and City
Council the agenda, previous meeting’s minutes, action items and any other
pertinent information regarding the scheduled meeting. This information is to
be delivered or mailed to the Mayor and City Council no later than the Friday
before the scheduled board or commission meeting.
   (D)   All city boards and commissions will have an agenda item for lobby
visitation. Additional agenda items are at the discretion of the board or
commission chairperson.
   (E)   Minutes from board and commission meetings will be forwarded to the
Clerk of Council within 12 working days after the board or commission meeting.
The Clerk of Council will distribute these minutes to the Mayor and City
Council (exceptions: Planning Commission, Board of Public Utilities, Civil
Service Commission and Zoning Board of Appeals, see division (C) above).
Minutes will be formally adopted in accordance with board or commission by-
laws.
   (F)   Special meetings are exempt from the requirements of divisions (B) and
(C). However, the Municipal Administrator’s office, or designated
representative, will notify the Mayor and City Council of the special board or
commission meeting.
(1980 Code, § 30.99) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 6444, passed 3-15-
1999)
§ 30.100 VACANCIES.
   Vacancies shall be filled for the unexpired term in the same manner as the
original appointment was made.
(1980 Code, § 30.100) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974)
§ 30.101 HISTORIC PRESERVATION COMMISSION.
   (A)   Establishment and purpose. The Historic Preservation Commission is
established to preserve, promote, encourage and support the maintenance, use
and reuse of historic buildings in the city. The purpose of the Commission is
to foster civic beauty, stabilize and increase property values, strengthen the
local economy, maintain and enhance the distinctive character, safeguard the
city's heritage, and facilitate reinvestment and revitalization through
historic preservation.
   (B)   Composition and appointment. The Commission shall consist of not less
than five nor more than seven members appointed by the Mayor subject to
confirmation by a majority of the members of Council and shall have all the
powers and duties provided in the charter, the state statutes, and the planning
and zoning-related codes. Members must be residents of the city, with at least
two members residing east of Main Street, at least two members residing west of
Main Street, and one member who owns a downtown building or a downtown
business. All members must have demonstrated a special interest, experience, or
knowledge in history, architecture, historic preservation, or related
disciplines. At least two members must be preservation related professionals to
the extent such professionals are available in the city. This shall include the
professions of architecture, architectural history, history, archaeology,
planning, or related discipline. Members' terms shall be four years. The
initial terms shall be established so the terms overlap: two members' terms
shall terminate in two years; two members' terms in three years; and one
member's term in four years.
   (C)   Organization. The Commission shall elect its own chairperson,
secretary, and such other officers as it deems advisable. The Commission shall
have full power to organize itself and to determine its own rules, regulations,
bylaws and meeting schedule. The Commission shall not meet less than four times
per year.
(Ord. 8714, passed 10-15-2018; Am. Ord. 8878, passed 3-15-2021)
§ 30.102 CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION.
   (A)   The Civil Service Commission shall prescribe, amend, and enforce rules
not inconsistent with R.C. §§ 124.01 through 124.64, for the classification of
positions in the civil service of the city. The Commission shall have the
powers and duties provided by statute except that when a vacancy occurs in the
classified service of the city, to be filled by appointment or promotion, the
Civil Service Commission shall certify to the appointing authority the names of
the three persons standing highest on the eligible list for the position and
the appointing officer shall appoint one of these persons to the position.
   (B)   The Commission shall consist of three members with six-year terms, not
more than two of whom shall be of the same political party. A member may be
removed as provided in R.C. § 124.40.
(1980 Code, § 30.102) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 3237, passed 1-20-
1975)

§ 30.105 HUMAN RELATIONS COMMISSION.
   The Human Relations Commission shall promote equality for and understanding
among all the people of the community and shall provide mediation through
conferences and conciliation. This Commission shall consist of nine members
with three-year terms. Additionally, one Bowling Green State University student
and one Bowling Green High School student shall be appointed to serve terms of
one year.
(1980 Code, § 30.105) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 6954, passed 5-6-

§ 30.106 PLANNING COMMISSION.
   The Planning Commission shall consist of nine members appointed by the Mayor
subject to confirmation by a majority of the members of Council and shall have
all the powers and duties provided in the charter, the state statutes, and the
planning and zoning code. At least four members shall be residents of the east
side of the city as divided by Main Street, and at least four members shall be
residents of the west side of the city so divided. The terms shall be staggered
so that the terms overlap so that one member’s term shall terminate in one
year; two members’ terms shall terminate in two years; one member’s term in
three years; two members’ terms in four years; one member’s term in five years;
and two members’ terms in six years. Thereafter, vacancies shall be filled for
appointments for the unexpired terms and the terms shall be for six years.
(1980 Code, § 30.106) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 3584, passed 5-16-

§ 30.107 RECORDS COMMISSION.
   (A)   There is hereby created in the City of Bowling Green a Records
Commission composed of the Mayor or the Mayor’s appointed representative, as
Chairperson, and the Finance Director, the City Attorney and a citizen
appointed by the Mayor. The Commission shall appoint a secretary, who is not be
a member of the Commission and who shall serve at the pleasure of the
Commission. The Commission may employ an archivist or records manager to serve
under its direction. The Commission shall meet at least once every six months
and upon the call of the Chairperson.
   (B)   The functions of the Commission shall be to provide rules for
retention and disposal of records of the City of Bowling Green, and to review
applications for one-time disposal of obsolete records and schedules of records
retention and disposition submitted by municipal offices. The Commission may
dispose of records pursuant to the procedure outlined in R.C. § 149.381. The
Commission, at any time, may review any schedule it has previously approved
and, for good cause shown, may revise that schedule under the procedure
outlined in that section.
(1980 Code, § 30.107) (Ord. 3073, passed 2-11-1974; Am. Ord. 5055, passed 8-7-
1989; Am. Ord. 6261, passed 1-20-1998; Am. Ord. 9147, passed 12-4-2023)

throughout the city with particular responsibility for the landscaping of city
property and shall educate and inform residents about the selection, planting
and maintenance of trees within the corporate limits, whether the same be on
private or public property, and shall consist of at least three persons but not
more than seven persons appointed by the Mayor with terms of three years.

§ 30.109 TRAFFIC COMMISSION.
   The Traffic Commission shall promote improved safety within the city and
review all traffic regulations made by the Safety Director. The Commission
shall consist of nine members, namely: the Police Chief, or his or her designee
when approved by the Mayor, the Fire Chief, or his or her designee when
approved by the Mayor, the Street Superintendent, or his or her designee when
approved by the Mayor, and six citizen members appointed by the Mayor to serve
four-year terms. At least two of the six persons serving by appointment of the
Mayor must reside on the east side of Main Street in the city. The Commission
shall have the authority to overrule temporary traffic regulations made by the
Safety Director.

§ 30.114 BOWLING GREEN HOUSING AGENCY.
   (A)   The Bowling Green Housing Agency is hereby created to oversee and
administrate the existing Section 8 Rental Assistance Program for the city.
   (B)   The Bowling Green Housing Agency shall be managed by a Board of
Trustees, which shall consist of five members, periodically appointed by the
Mayor, to represent health care providers and other professionals. The terms of
office for each trustee shall be four years. The term of office for the first
two appointments shall terminate after two years, for the third appointment in
three years, and for the fourth and fifth appointments in four years, and
thereafter, all terms shall expire four years after appointment. Terms as
trustee shall be limited to two successive terms or ten years of service,
whichever is longer. Once a member has served on the agency for the maximum
successive time permitted herein, a discontinuance of service for at least one
year shall be required before the former member may be reappointed as a trustee
for a new term.
   (C)   The Board of Trustees shall organize annually by electing a
chairperson, a vice-chairperson and a secretary, and such other officers as it
deems convenient. The Board shall annually, or as it sees fit, adopt rules for
the transaction of business and keep a journal of its proceedings and minutes.
   (D)   Meetings of the Board of Trustees shall be called on an as needed
basis by the chairperson, or the Mayor, or by three members of the Board of
Trustees. A majority of the Board of Trustees shall constitute a quorum for the
transaction of business.
   (E)   Meetings of the Board of Trustees at which any final action is to be
taken or a decision rendered shall be open to the public, and any action taken
or a decision rendered at any meeting from which members of the public are
excluded, except for misconduct, shall be void.
   (F)   Vacancies on the Board of Trustees shall be filled for unexpired term
in the same manner as the original appointment was made.
(1980 Code, § 30.93) (Ord. 5724, passed 7-5-1994)
§ 30.115 SIDEWALK COMMISSION.
   (A)   The Sidewalk Commission shall determine those locations of the city
that need sidewalk repair or new sidewalk construction. The recommendations
shall be based on pedestrian safety. The priority list shall be subject to
available city funds as appropriated in each calendar year.
   (B)   The Commission shall consist of eight members, namely: the Safety
Director, a member of the Traffic Commission, a member of the Transportation
and Safety Committee of the City Council and five citizen members appointed by
the Mayor to serve four-year terms. At least two members shall be residents of
the east side of the city as divided by Main Street, and at least two members
shall be residents of the west side of the city so divided.
(1980 Code, § 30.115) (Ord. 4456, passed 7-16-1984; Am. Ord. 5055, passed 8-7-
1989; Am. Ord. 6959, passed 5-6-2002; Am. Ord. 8780, passed 7-15-2019; Am. Ord.
9292, passed 7-21-2025)
§ 30.116 BICYCLE SAFETY COMMISSION.
   (A)   There is hereby created and established a Bicycle Safety Commission
for the city, which shall consist of nine members appointed by the Mayor
including: a representative from the Police Division; a representative from the
Parks and Recreation Department; a Bowling Green State University student; a
Bowling Green High School student; a Bowling Green Junior High School student.
At least two members shall be residents of the east side of the city as divided
by Main Street, and four citizen members appointed by the Mayor. Of the four
citizen members, at least two members shall be residents of the east side of
the city as divided by Main Street, and at least two members shall be residents
of the west side of the city so divided.
   (B)   The terms of student members shall be for one year. Terms for all
other members shall be three years. Implementation of three-year terms will be
effective June 1, 2008. To properly transition to alternating three-year terms,
the following terms will be applied: terms number one and two to expire on May
31, 2009; terms three and four to expire on May 31, 2010; and terms five and
six to expire on May 31, 2011; thereafter, all terms to extend three years.
   (C)   The powers and duties of this Commission shall include but not be
limited solely to, developing and implementing bicycle safety educational
projects to be conducted in the schools and elsewhere and directed toward both
adults and juveniles; identifying and recommending the establishment of
recognizable bicycle routes and bike-ways throughout the local area;
conceiving, arranging, scheduling, and conducting bicycle safety checks,
demonstrations, and participatory events, both competitive and noncompetitive;
recommending appropriate bicycle safety legislation to the city administration
or legislative authority, encouraging the enforcement of state laws and city
ordinances pertaining to the ownership and operation of bicycles; working with
local service clubs and other interested agencies as required to ensure
coordination of effort toward a total bicycle program; and promoting bicycle
safety by obtaining maximum publicity for the goals and programs developed by
the Commission, and by participating as required in meetings, conferences,
seminars, and workshops. This Commission may also be delegated other specific
or general powers or functions by the Council of the city.
   (D)   This Commission shall organize annually to elect a chairperson, vice-
chairperson, and secretary. Meetings shall be held at the call of the
chairperson and at such other times as the Commission shall determine.
      (1)   A majority of the members present shall constitute a quorum for the
transaction of business. The Commission shall adopt rules for the transaction
of business and keep a journal of its proceedings.
      (2)   The Commission may call upon the various departments of the city
for assistance in the performance of its duties, and it shall be the duty of
such departments to render such assistance to the Commission as may be
reasonably required.
(1980 Code, § 30.116) (Ord. 5788, passed 11-21-1994; Am. Ord. 6824, passed 7-
16-2001; Am. Ord. 6960, passed 5-6-2002; Am. Ord. 7449, passed 9-6-2005; Am.
Ord. 7592, passed 9-5-2006)
§ 30.117 CITY-UNIVERSITY RELATIONS COMMISSION.
   (A)   Establishment. A City-University Relations Commission is hereby
created consisting of 12 members in accordance with the following:
   (B)   Composition and appointment. The composition of the Commission and
method of appointment thereto shall be as follows:
      (1)   Four Bowling Green State University (BGSU) students, at least one
of whom shall be a graduate student, and each of whom shall serve for a term of
one academic year. Terms shall be staggered, with two of the initial student
representatives serving a term of three academic semesters. Representatives
shall be appointed jointly by the Undergraduate Student Government and Graduate
Student Senate.
      (2)   Three Bowling Green residents, at least two of whom shall reside
east of Main Street, and each of whom shall serve for a term of two years.
Terms shall be staggered, with two of the initial resident representatives
serving a term of one year. Representatives shall be appointed by the Mayor.
      (3)   (a)   Five ex officio members, each of whom will serve for a term
of two years:
            1.   One member of the City Council, to be appointed by the Mayor;
            2.   One representative of the local neighborhood association, to
be appointed by that association;
            3.   One member of the local landlord community, to be appointed by
that community;
            4.   One representative of the City of Bowling Green, to be
appointed by the Mayor; and
            5.   One representative of BGSU, to be appointed by the President
of BGSU.
         (b)   Terms shall be staggered, with the initial members representing
the neighborhood association and landlord community serving a term of one year.
   (C)   Organization. The Commission shall elect its own chairperson,
secretary, and such other officers as it deems advisable. The Commission shall
have full power to organize itself and to determine its own rules, regulations,
and bylaws. The Commission shall meet not less than once per month during the
academic year at a regularly scheduled time, date, and place.
   (D)   Purpose. The purpose of the Commission shall be to serve as a forum to
address recurring issues that arise between students and city residents, and
may also impact other city and campus constituencies, including city employees
and officials, and university administrators, faculty, and staff; and to
thereby improve relations between these constituencies through inclusivity,
collaboration, authentic dialogue, and policy recommendation. Issues that may
be addressed by the Commission include, but are not limited to, neighborly
conduct, student housing, nuisance parties, trash and litter, parking, drug and
alcohol concerns, property crimes, and general disorderly behavior.
   (E)   Duties and responsibilities. The Commission shall work to diminish
negative stereotypes of city and campus constituencies, research best practices
regarding city-university relations and consult with other college towns,
solicit public input and feedback, and foster civic engagement on these issues.
The Commission shall serve as a venue for authentic dialogue and civic
discourse and education, encourage community-wide investment in city and campus
affairs, and promote collaborative approaches to public problem solving through
coordination of stakeholders. The Commission shall report and recommend or
propose policy changes to the city and/or university, as the Commission deems
necessary and appropriate under the circumstances. The Commission is expressly
authorized and directed to make such recommendations and proposals relative to
legislation or policy matters as the Commission determines to be in the
interest of city-university relations.
(Ord. 8324, passed 4-21-2014)

§ 31.01 REGULAR MEETINGS.
   Regular meetings shall be held in the Council Chamber on the first and third
Monday of each month at such time as determined by City Council. When the date
of any meeting falls on a legal holiday or an election day, Council shall meet
on the following day at the same hour. Council may dispense with any regular
meeting or change the day and hour of holding any regular meeting.
(1980 Code, § 31.01) (Am. Ord. 8244, passed 6-3-2013)
Charter reference:
   Meetings, see Charter, §
2.09
§ 31.02 SPECIAL MEETINGS.
   Special meetings may be called by a vote of the Council taken at any regular
or special meeting thereof, or shall be called by the Clerk upon the written
request of the Mayor or president of Council or of three members of Council.
Any such request shall state the time, place, and date thereof and the subject
or subjects to be considered at the meeting, and no other subject or subjects
shall be considered. Notice in writing of each such special meeting called,
except by vote of Council, shall be given to each member of Council and the
Mayor by serving the same on each of them personally or by leaving a copy
thereof at his or her usual place of residence not less than 24 hours prior to
the meeting. Service of notice may be waived in writing and shall be deemed
conclusively to be waived by attendance at the special meeting. In the event
that a special meeting is called by a vote of Council at a meeting from which
the Mayor or any member of Council is absent, written notice of the special
meeting shall be given each absentee in the manner hereinbefore described.
(1980 Code, § 31.02) (Am. Ord. 4409, passed 2-21-1984)
Charter reference:
   Meetings, see Charter, §
2.09
§ 31.03 QUORUM.
   A majority (four votes) of all members elected to Council shall be necessary
to constitute a quorum.
(1980 Code, § 31.03)
Charter reference:

2.06
§ 31.04 ORDER OF BUSINESS.
   Unless otherwise ordered by Council, the following shall be the order of
business at all regular sessions of Council.
   (A)   Pledge of allegiance.
   (B)   Roll call.
   (C)   Approval of minutes.
   (D)   Correspondence received by Clerk.
   (E)    Special recognition(s), if any.
   (F)   Lobby visitations.
   (G)   Introduction of new legislation.
   (H)   Official reports by the Mayor and City Officers.
   (I)   Council committee reports.
   (J)   Ordinances and resolutions for first reading.
   (K)   Ordinances and resolutions for second reading.
   (L)   Ordinances and resolutions for third reading.
   (M)   Ordinances and resolutions which may be tabled.
   (N)   Any other business legitimately presented to Council.
(1980 Code, § 31.04) (Am. Ord. 4409, passed 2-21-1984; Am. Ord. 9161, passed 2-
20-2024)
§ 31.05 STANDING COMMITTEES.
   The following standing committees, consisting of three members each, and the
first member named to be the chairperson of each such committee, shall be
appointed by the President of Council at the first meeting in January of each
term or as soon as may be practicable thereafter.
   (A)   Finance and Ways and Means. Whose duty it shall be to examine into and
report upon all matters of accounts or claims against or in favor of the city,
to prepare and approve the semi-annual appropriations ordinances, to examine
and report upon all matters relative to the revenue of the city which may be
referred to it, to fix the tax level for the several general funds from the
annual budgets for the city officers, to inquire into the city debts, the
revenue and expenditures and whether any and what retrenchment can be made at
any time to advantage, and to report from time to time upon those provisions
and arrangements which are conducive to economy, order, and accountability in
the conduct of the fiscal affairs of the city.
   (B)   Transportation and Safety. Whose duty it shall be to take into
consideration all matters pertaining to parking, traffic control, streets and
alleys, Fire Division, Police Division, and related matters.
   (C)   Public Utilities Committee. Whose duty it shall be to consider all
matters pertaining to electric, water, sewer, and to make suggestions regarding
service and the regulation of same, and to report upon those matters referred
to it. Also includes cable TV contract.
   (D)   Planning, Zoning and Economic Development.  Whose duty it shall be to
consider and report on all matters pertaining to the planning, zoning,
industrial and economic development of the city.
   (E)   Parks, Recreation, Public Lands and Buildings. Whose duty it shall be
to consider and report upon matters pertaining to parks and recreation services
and matters pertaining to lands or buildings owned or used by the city other
than those used by the Utilities Department.
   (F)   Sustainability. Whose duty it shall be to consider and report on
matters relating to sustainability initiatives and related matters.
   (G)   Community Improvement. Whose duty it shall be to consider and report
upon all matters pertaining to litter control; vandalism; loud parties;
neighborhood associations; municipal employee attitudes; animal control; drug
and alcohol concerns; and related matters.
(1980 Code, § 31.05) (Am. Ord. 3759, passed 9-5-1978; Am. Ord. 4409, passed 2-
21-1984; Am. Ord. 5946, passed 1-16-1996; Am. Ord. 8900, passed 2-16-2021)
§ 31.06 COMMITTEES SUBJECT TO CALL.
   All standing committees shall be subject to the call of the chairperson of
each committee or the president of Council.
(1980 Code, § 31.06)
§ 31.07 COMMITTEE REPORT.
   Committees shall report on all matters referred to them as soon as feasible.
(1980 Code, § 31.07) (Am. Ord. 4409, passed 2-21-1984)
§ 31.08 COMMITTEE MEETING ABSENTEEISM.
   Any member of any committee who shall absent himself or herself from two or
more successive committee meetings, except in case of sickness or absence from
the city, may be removed from that committee by the president of Council upon a
two-thirds vote of the members elected to Council, and Council, by two-thirds
vote, may also declare the member not eligible to any further committeeship.
(1980 Code, § 31.08)
§ 31.09 NAMING AND/OR RENAMING OF CITY OWNED FACILITIES.
   City Council shall have the power to name and/or rename city owned public
facilities in accordance with rules and regulations promulgated by the Mayor
and Municipal Administrator from time to time.
(1980 Code, § 31.09) (Ord. 6056, passed 10-7-1996)
§ 31.10 ENDORSEMENT ON LEGISLATION.
   All legislation recommended for passage or otherwise by the head of
departments or committees shall be so endorsed on the back thereof.
(1980 Code, § 31.10)
§ 31.11 REFERENCE TO COMMITTEE.
   A motion to refer to a standing committee shall take precedence over a
similar motion for a special committee. (1980 Code, § 31.11)
§ 31.12 MOTIONS.
   Every motion shall be reduced to writing, if the president or member making
the motion so desires, except a motion to adjourn, postpone, or commit. When
made or seconded, the motion shall be stated by the president, or, if written,
shall be read by the Clerk.
(1980 Code, § 31.12)
§ 31.13 VOTING.
   Every member who shall be present when a question is put shall vote thereon,
unless excused by Council or unless he or she is directly interested in the
question, in which case he or she shall not vote. The yeas and nays shall be
called on request of the chair or any member of Council.
(1980 Code, § 31.13)
§ 31.14 INTRODUCTION OF LEGISLATION.
   Resolutions and ordinances can be introduced only by a member of Council,
when present, and with his or her name endorsed thereon, or by a committee
report with its endorsement thereon.
(1980 Code, § 31.14)
Charter reference:
   Ordinances and resolutions, see Charter, §
2.10
§ 31.15 INVESTIGATION OF EXPENDITURE OR ASSESSMENT.
   All communications, resolutions, and ordinances contemplating or providing
for the expenditure of public funds or assessments upon property owners shall
be referred to the appropriate committee or the Council member of the
respective ward for investigation and recommendation before they can be
considered by Council.
(1980 Code, § 31.15)
§ 31.16 FINANCE DIRECTOR CERTIFICATE ON EXPENDITURES.
   No contract, agreement, or other object involving the expenditure of money
shall be entered into, nor shall any ordinance, resolution, or order for the
appropriation or expenditure of money be passed by Council unless the Finance
Director shall have first certified that the money required for the contract,
agreement, or other obligation, or to pay the appropriation or expenditure, is
in the treasury to the credit of the fund on which it is to be drawn and not
appropriated for any other purpose. However, this rule does not apply to
special improvements to be raised by assessment of property owners or for which
an issue of bonds is to be provided.
(1980 Code, § 31.16)
§ 31.17 VOTE ON SPECIAL ASSESSMENT.
   To pass ordinances or resolutions for any improvement or other matter, the
cost or part of the cost of which is to be paid by special assessments, a
three-fourths vote of all members elected to Council (six votes) shall be
necessary, unless a petition by property owners is presented therefor according
to law.
(1980 Code, § 31.17)
§ 31.18 READINGS ON LEGISLATION.
   All bylaws, ordinances, and resolutions shall be fully and distinctly read
on three different regular meeting days, unless, by three-fourths vote (six
votes) of Council elected thereto, Council shall dispense with the rule.
However, this rule shall not apply to the ordering of an election or the
direction by Council to any city officers or board to furnish Council with
information as to the affairs of any department of the city, or resolution
instructing investigation or reports from officers.
(1980 Code, § 31.18)
§ 31.19 AMENDMENTS.
   If amendments to any resolution or ordinance are offered and adopted, the
chair shall so report and the ordinance shall be read as amended on request of
any member before the vote on its passage is taken, but no amendment shall be
offered until the resolution or ordinance shall be read the second time.
(1980 Code, § 31.19)
§ 31.20 MOTION TO RECONSIDER.
   A motion to reconsider a vote must be made by a member voting on the
prevailing side, and the motion shall be made at the same meeting of Council.
No motion to reconsider shall be made more than once on any matter or subject,
and the same number of votes shall be required to reconsider any action of
Council required to pass or adopt the same.
(1980 Code, § 31.20)
§ 31.21 FRANCHISE, EXPENDITURE, OR TAX LEVY.
   All ordinances or resolutions granting a franchise, creating a right, or
involving the expenditure of money or the levying of any tax, or for purchase,
lease, sale, or transfer of property, shall not be passed unless the same shall
have been read on three different days and, with respect to any such ordinance
or resolution, there shall be no authority to dispense with this rule except by
a three-fourths vote (six votes) of all members elected thereto. No ordinance
or resolution can be passed without the concurrence of a majority (four votes)
of all members elected thereto, and the vote on the ordinance or resolution
shall be taken by “yeas” and “nays” and so recorded upon the journal.
(1980 Code, § 31.21)
Charter reference:
   Publishing ordinance or resolution in newspaper, see Charter, §

§ 31.22 ENROLLMENT OF ORDINANCE.
   After an ordinance shall have passed, it shall be enrolled by the Clerk in
an ordinance book kept for that purpose. After having been checked, it shall be
signed by the president or presiding officer and the Clerk.
(1980 Code, § 31.22)
§ 31.23 EXTENDED UNEXCUSED ABSENCE FROM COUNCIL.
   Any member who, without valid excuse, sickness, or leave of absence, absents
himself or herself from six consecutive sessions of Council, extending over a
period of at least two months, may be expelled from Council by a vote of two-
thirds of all members elected thereto.
(1980 Code, § 31.23)
§ 31.24 ADOPTION OF COMMITTEE REPORTS.
   It shall require a majority of all members elected to adopt a committee
report.
(1980 Code, § 31.24)
§ 31.25 ADOPTION OF MOTIONS.
   A majority of all members present at any session shall be necessary to the
adoption of any motion.
(1980 Code, § 31.25)
§ 31.26 CALLING THE ROLL.
   In taking the yeas and nays, the Clerk shall list the members’ names in
alphabetical order with numbers assigned to each Council member 1 through 7.
      (1)   The first roll call after adoption of this section shall be called
in the following order: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7.
      (2)   The next roll call shall be called in the following order: 2, 3, 4,
5, 6, 7, 1.
      (3)   The next roll call shall be called in the following order: 3, 4, 5,
6, 7, 1, 2.
      (4)   The next roll call shall be called in the following order: 4, 5, 6,
7, 1, 2, 3.
      (5)   The next roll call shall be called in the following order: 5, 6, 7,
1, 2, 3, 4.
      (6)   The next roll call shall be called in the following order: 6, 7, 1,
2, 3, 4, 5.
      (7)   The next roll call shall be called in the following order: 7, 1, 2,
3, 4, 5, 6.
   (B)   In all ensuing roll calls, the above rotating order shall be used by
the Clerk in taking roll call votes.
(1980 Code, § 31.26) (Ord. 4577, passed 8-19-1985)
§ 31.27 VOTING WITHOUT ROLL CALL.
   Upon all questions before Council upon which no yea or nay vote is required
or taken, the president, after putting the question, shall declare all votes
and, if in doubt, may direct that a rising vote be taken, or any member can
call for a division.
(1980 Code, § 31.27)
§ 31.28 FINAL REPORT.
   Every final report of a committee can be either oral or written at the
option of the committee.
(1980 Code, § 31.28) (Am. Ord. 4409, passed 2-21-1984)
§ 31.29 MOTION TO ADJOURN.
   A motion to adjourn shall always be in order except when a vote is being
taken and shall not be debatable.
(1980 Code, § 31.29)
§ 31.30 PRECEDENCE OF MOTIONS.
   When a question is under debate no motion shall be in order except to
adjourn, lay on the table, postpone to the next meeting, commit, amend, or
postpone indefinitely, which several motions shall have precedence in the order
in which they are herein stated.
(1980 Code, § 31.30)
§ 31.31 FINANCE DIRECTOR MONTHLY REPORT.
   The Finance Director shall, at the second regular meeting of each month,
render a detailed statement to Council of the receipt and expenditures of the
several officers and departments for the preceding month.
(1980 Code, § 31.31)
§ 31.32 DUTIES OF CLERK.
   It shall be the duty of the Clerk to keep a correct journal of the
proceedings of Council, to cause Council’s committee members and officers and
city officers and departments to be informed of those duties they may be
charged with by Council from time to time, and perform those other duties which
appertain to him or her as Clerk. He or she shall permit no journal accounts or
papers to be taken from his or her files or out of his or her custody other
than by the regular mode of business of Council, and if any paper in his or her
charge shall be missing he or she shall make a report to Council forthwith so
that the matter may be inquired into. He or she shall also act as Clerk of all
improvement committees which may desire his or her services.
(1980 Code, § 31.32)

   These rules shall not be altered except by a two-thirds vote of all members
of Council elected thereto and at a regular meeting. The proposition to make an
amendment shall be in the form of a resolution and shall be submitted and read
to Council at a meeting preceding the one at which it is acted on.
(1980 Code, § 31.33)
§ 31.34 SUSPENSION OF RULES.

elected to Council.
(1980 Code, § 31.34)

   (B)   The compensation for the Clerk of Council for his or her regular

§ 31.37 SALARY AND DUTIES OF COUNCILPERSONS.
   (A)   The salary of the president of Council shall be as set by legislative
authority, payable in 12 equal monthly installments from the general fund. The
president of Council shall have those duties as are provided by the Ohio
Revised Code.
   (B)   The annual salary of the Members of Bowling Green City Council shall
align with the minimum earnable salary for one-year service credit as

(1980 Code, § 31.37) (Ord. 2277, passed 12-19-1966; Am. Ord. 4825, passed 12-
